title: Praggnanandhaa Takes Sole Lead at Saint Louis Rapid and Blitz
excerpt: India's 21-year-old grandmaster scored 12 points in the rapid segment to lead the fourth leg of the Grand Chess Tour, with the blitz portion still to come.
body:
• R Praggnanandhaa scored 12 points in the rapid portion to take the sole lead at the 2026 Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz, one point ahead of Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov
  • The event is the fourth leg of the Grand Chess Tour, with 18 rounds of blitz still to be played before a final winner is determined
  • Praggnanandhaa, a 2026 World Championship Candidates qualifier, has won Norway Chess and the Tata Steel tournament this year

Dominant in St. Louis

R Praggnanandhaa has stamped his authority on the 2026 Saint Louis Rapid & Blitz, completing the rapid portion with 12 points out of a possible 18 to take the sole lead in the fourth leg of the Grand Chess Tour. The 21-year-old Indian grandmaster finished a full point clear of his nearest rival, Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, who scored 11.

American favourite Wesley So sits third on 10 points, while four players — Leinier Domínguez, Anish Giri, Vincent Keymer, and Levon Aronian — share fourth place on 9 points each. Fabiano Caruana, the current Grand Chess Tour points leader, and Jorden van Foreest are tied for eighth on 8 points.

"Blitz to Decide It While Praggnanandhaa's one-point lead is comfortable, the blitz portion can produce dramatic swings."

The event, running August 2-6 in St. Louis, Missouri, features nine rounds of rapid chess followed by 18 rounds of blitz. The rapid segment uses a time control of 25 minutes plus a 10-second increment, with wins worth 2 points and draws 1. The blitz portion, which begins on the tournament's final days, uses a 5+2 time control with 1 point for a win.

A Remarkable Year for Pragg

Praggnanandhaa's performance in St. Louis extends what has been a remarkable 2026 campaign. The Chennai-born grandmaster has already claimed the 2026 Norway Chess title and qualified for the World Championship Candidates cycle. His 2025 was equally impressive, winning both the Tata Steel Chess Tournament and the Superbet Chess Classic in Romania.

With a FIDE standard rating of 2750, Praggnanandhaa has established himself as one of the world's elite players. His rapid and blitz credentials are equally strong — he finished joint third at the previous Grand Chess Tour event in Zagreb, Croatia, behind the dominant Alireza Firouzja.

The Field and the Stakes

The Saint Louis event carries particular significance for the overall Grand Chess Tour standings. Caruana leads the tour with 20 points from two events, followed by Germany's Vincent Keymer on 19. A strong finish could vault Praggnanandhaa — currently fifth in the tour on 11.5 points — into contention for the top four, which qualifies for the lucrative GCT Finals later in August.

Notably absent is France's Firouzja, who withdrew from the Sinquefield Cup (and thus the overall tour) due to a scheduling conflict with the chess tournament at the Esports World Cup. His absence opens the field but also removes the player who has been the most dangerous in rapid and blitz formats this season.

World champion Gukesh Dommaraju also opted out of the St. Louis rapid and blitz after withdrawing from the full tour earlier in the year, citing a desire to reduce his playing schedule following a stretch of poor results.

Blitz to Decide It

While Praggnanandhaa's one-point lead is comfortable, the blitz portion can produce dramatic swings. At the previous Grand Chess Tour event in Croatia, Firouzja scored 8 out of 9 on a single day of blitz to storm into an insurmountable lead, demonstrating how quickly rapid standings can be overturned.

Sindarov, the reigning FIDE World Cup champion and 2026 Candidates Tournament winner, has the blitz firepower to challenge for first. So does Wesley So, a three-time Grand Chess Tour champion with extensive experience in St. Louis, his adopted home city.

For Praggnanandhaa, the challenge is clear: convert the rapid lead into an overall victory. A win in St. Louis would strengthen his position for the GCT Finals and add another title to a season that has already cemented his status as India's leading chess prospect since Viswanathan Anand.
